lessons.title: What is CSS?
objectives: Learn the three ways to apply CSS
lessons.content: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) controls the visual presentation of HTML — colors, spacing, fonts, and layout. It can be applied inline, internally, or via an external stylesheet.
lessons.notes: External stylesheets are preferred for maintainability.
lessons.mistakes: Overusing inline styles makes a page hard to maintain.
lessons.practice: Style a heading's color using an external-style approach in this editor.
lessons.challenge: Change the font-family of your paragraph text.

quiz.question: What does CSS control?
options: The visual presentation: colours, spacing, fonts, layout

hint.en: CSS stands for Cascading STYLE Sheets.

explanation.en: CSS handles how HTML looks. HTML gives structure.
explanation.sw: CSS hushughulikia muonekano wa HTML. HTML hutoa muundo.

quiz.question: Which way of adding CSS is preferred for real projects?

hint.en: Think about maintaining 50 pages at once.
hint.sw: Fikiria kutunza kurasa 50 kwa wakati mmoja.

explanation.en: One external file styles many pages and is easy to maintain.
explanation.sw: Faili moja la nje linapamba kurasa nyingi na ni rahisi kutunza.

quiz.question: What does this rule do?

hint.en: h1 is the selector; color is the property.
hint.sw: h1 ni selector; color ni property.

explanation.en: The h1 selector targets all h1 elements, and color sets their text colour.
explanation.sw: Selector ya h1 inalenga h1 zote, na color huweka rangi ya maandishi.

lessons.title: Selectors
objectives: Use element, class and id selectors
lessons.content: Selectors target which elements a rule applies to. Element selectors target tags, class selectors (.name) target groups, and id selectors (#name) target a single element.
lessons.notes: Prefer classes over ids for styling — ids carry high specificity and are harder to override.
lessons.mistakes: Overusing id selectors, making later overrides painful.
lessons.practice: Style two paragraphs differently using two separate classes.
lessons.challenge: Combine a class and element selector, e.g. p.intro.

quiz.question: Which selector targets elements with class="intro"?

explanation.en: .name selects classes, #name selects ids.
explanation.sw: .jina huchagua class, #jina huchagua id.

quiz.question: How many elements should one id normally belong to?

explanation.en: An id must be unique on the page; classes can be reused.
explanation.sw: id lazima iwe ya kipekee kwenye ukurasa; class zinaweza kutumika tena.

quiz.question: Why prefer classes over ids for styling?
options: Ids are not allowed in CSS
Ids have high specificity and are harder to override

hint.en: Think about which one wins in a conflict.

explanation.en: High specificity makes ids hard to override later.
explanation.sw: Specificity ya juu hufanya id iwe ngumu kubatilisha baadaye.

lessons.title: Colors & Typography
objectives: Apply color using hex, rgb and named values
lessons.content: Colors can be defined with keywords, hex codes, or rgb()/rgba(). Typography properties include font-family, font-size, font-weight and line-height.
lessons.notes: rgba() lets you add transparency to a color.
lessons.mistakes: Using too many font families on one page hurts consistency.
lessons.practice: Style a paragraph with a custom color, size and line-height.
lessons.challenge: Add a semi-transparent background using rgba().

quiz.question: Which is a valid way to write a colour?

hint.en: A hash followed by hex digits.
hint.sw: Alama ya # ikifuatiwa na tarakimu za hex.

explanation.en: Hex codes start with # and use 3 or 6 hex digits.
explanation.sw: Hex huanza na # na hutumia tarakimu 3 au 6.

quiz.question: What does rgba(0,0,0,0.5) add compared to rgb()?

explanation.en: The alpha value (0 to 1) controls opacity.
explanation.sw: Thamani ya alpha (0 hadi 1) hudhibiti uwazi.

quiz.question: Which property sets the space between lines of text?

hint.en: It is about the height of each line.

explanation.en: line-height sets line spacing; 1.5 to 1.6 reads comfortably.
explanation.sw: line-height huweka nafasi ya mistari; 1.5 hadi 1.6 husomeka vizuri.

lessons.title: The Box Model
objectives: Understand content, padding, border and margin
lessons.content: Every HTML element is a box made of content, padding, border, and margin. box-sizing: border-box makes width/height include padding and border, which is far more predictable.
lessons.notes: Setting box-sizing: border-box globally avoids many layout headaches.
lessons.mistakes: Forgetting that default box-sizing adds padding on top of the set width.
lessons.practice: Give a card element padding, a border, and a margin.
lessons.challenge: Switch box-sizing to border-box and observe the difference.

quiz.question: Which list shows the box model layers from inside to outside?

hint.en: Start at the text and move outward.
hint.sw: Anza kwenye maandishi kisha nenda nje.

explanation.en: Content is surrounded by padding, then border, then margin.
explanation.sw: Content imezungukwa na padding, kisha border, kisha margin.

quiz.question: With box-sizing: border-box, width: 200px means:
options: Total box including padding and border is 200px
Content is 200px, padding added on top

hint.en: It makes the sizing more predictable.

explanation.en: border-box includes padding and border inside the width.
explanation.sw: border-box inajumuisha padding na border ndani ya width.

quiz.question: Which property adds space OUTSIDE the border?

hint.en: Padding is inside, so the other one is outside.
hint.sw: Padding ni ndani, kwa hiyo nyingine ni nje.

explanation.en: margin separates the element from its neighbours.
explanation.sw: margin hutenganisha kipengele na jirani zake.

lessons.title: Display & Positioning
objectives: Understand block vs inline vs inline-block
lessons.content: The display property controls how an element participates in layout: block elements stack, inline elements flow with text, inline-block combines both behaviors. Position controls how elements shift out of normal flow.
lessons.notes: position: absolute needs a positioned ancestor (relative/absolute/fixed) to behave predictably.
lessons.mistakes: Using position:absolute everywhere instead of standard layout flow.
lessons.practice: Turn a list of links into inline-block navigation items.
lessons.challenge: Position a small badge in the corner of a card using absolute positioning.

quiz.question: How do block elements behave?
options: They flow inside a line of text
They start on a new line and take full width

hint.en: Think of a div or a paragraph.

explanation.en: Block elements stack vertically and fill the available width.
explanation.sw: Block hupangwa chini kwa chini na kujaza upana unaopatikana.

quiz.question: What does position: absolute need to behave predictably?
options: A positioned ancestor (relative, absolute or fixed)

hint.en: It positions itself relative to something.

explanation.en: Without a positioned ancestor it uses the page as reference.
explanation.sw: Bila babu aliyepangwa, hutumia ukurasa kama rejea.

quiz.question: What does display: inline-block allow?
options: Flowing with text while accepting width, height and padding

explanation.en: inline-block flows like inline but behaves like a box.
explanation.sw: inline-block hutiririka kama inline lakini hufanya kazi kama kisanduku.

lessons.title: Flexbox Basics
lessons.content: Flexbox arranges items in a row or column. display:flex on a parent, then justify-content and align-items control alignment of its children.
lessons.notes: Flexbox is ideal for one-dimensional layouts like navbars and card rows.
lessons.mistakes: Forgetting display:flex on the parent before using flex properties.
lessons.practice: Build a horizontal navbar using flexbox with space-between.
lessons.challenge: Center a single item both horizontally and vertically using flexbox.

quiz.question: Which declaration turns a parent into a flex container?

hint.en: It is a value of display.

explanation.en: display:flex activates flexbox on the children.
explanation.sw: display:flex huwasha flexbox kwa watoto.

quiz.question: Which property spaces flex items along the main axis (e.g. between)?

explanation.en: justify-content distributes items on the main axis.
explanation.sw: justify-content husambaza vipengele kwenye mhimili mkuu.

quiz.question: What is flexbox best at?

hint.en: Think of a row of buttons.

explanation.en: Flexbox lays out in a row OR a column.
explanation.sw: Flexbox hupanga kwa safu AU safu wima.

lessons.title: Grid Basics
lessons.content: CSS Grid arranges items in two dimensions. display:grid combined with grid-template-columns defines your layout structure.
lessons.notes: Grid excels at whole-page layouts; flexbox excels at single rows or columns.
lessons.mistakes: Trying to force complex 2D layouts using only flexbox.
lessons.practice: Create a 3-column grid of cards with equal spacing.
lessons.challenge: Make one card span two columns using grid-column.

quiz.question: What does this create?

hint.en: fr means a fraction of free space.
hint.sw: fr ni sehemu ya nafasi iliyobaki.

explanation.en: repeat(3,1fr) makes three equal-width columns.
explanation.sw: repeat(3,1fr) hutengeneza safu wima tatu zenye upana sawa.

quiz.question: Which property sets the space between grid items?

explanation.en: gap sets row and column gutters.
explanation.sw: gap huweka nafasi kati ya safu na safu wima.

quiz.question: Grid is best for:

explanation.en: Grid controls rows and columns at the same time.
explanation.sw: Grid hudhibiti safu na safu wima kwa wakati mmoja.

lessons.title: Responsive Basics
lessons.content: Responsive design adapts layout to screen size using relative units (%, rem, vw) and media queries that apply styles conditionally.
lessons.notes: Design mobile-first: base styles for small screens, then enhance for larger ones.
lessons.mistakes: Using fixed pixel widths that overflow on small screens.
lessons.practice: Make a container full-width below 600px using a media query.
lessons.challenge: Stack a two-column layout into one column on mobile.

quiz.question: Which unit scales relative to the root font size?

explanation.en: rem is relative to the html font-size.
explanation.sw: rem inahusiana na font-size ya html.

quiz.question: What does this do?
options: Applies only on screens 600px wide or less

hint.en: max-width means up to that width.

explanation.en: Media queries apply styles conditionally by screen size.
explanation.sw: Media query hutumia mitindo kwa masharti ya ukubwa wa skrini.

quiz.question: What does mobile-first mean?
options: Write base styles for small screens, then enhance for larger ones

explanation.en: You add min-width queries to enhance larger screens.
explanation.sw: Unaongeza min-width kuboresha skrini kubwa.

lessons.title: Pseudo-classes & Transitions
lessons.content: Pseudo-classes like :hover and :focus style elements based on user interaction. The transition property smooths changes between states.
lessons.notes: Always style :focus for keyboard accessibility, not just :hover.
lessons.mistakes: Relying only on :hover, which excludes keyboard and touch users.
lessons.practice: Add a hover effect that changes a button's background color smoothly.
lessons.challenge: Add a focus-visible outline style to the same button.

quiz.question: Which pseudo-class styles an element when the mouse is over it?

hint.en: The name is literally the action.

explanation.en: :hover applies while the pointer is over the element.
explanation.sw: :hover hutumika pointer ikiwa juu ya kipengele.

quiz.question: Why style :focus too?
options: Keyboard users need to see where they are

explanation.en: Focus styles are vital for keyboard accessibility.
explanation.sw: Mtindo wa focus ni muhimu kwa ufikivu wa kibodi.

quiz.question: What does transition do?

hint.en: Think of animating a hover change.

explanation.en: transition animates property changes over time.
explanation.sw: transition huhuisha mabadiliko ya property kwa muda.

lessons.title: Building a Styled Card
objectives: Combine box model, flexbox and color into a component
lessons.content: You'll now combine everything: box model, color, flexbox and hover states to build a complete, polished course card component.
lessons.notes: Small, reusable components are the building blocks of real interfaces.
lessons.mistakes: Over-engineering a single component before it needs the complexity.
lessons.practice: Build a card with an image, title, description and a styled button.
lessons.challenge: Add a subtle lift animation to the card on hover.

quiz.question: In the card, what does transform: translateY(-4px) on hover do?

explanation.en: translateY moves vertically; negative is upward.
explanation.sw: translateY husogeza wima; hasi ni juu.

quiz.question: Why build small reusable components?
options: They are building blocks of real interfaces

hint.en: Think of reusing a card many times.

explanation.en: Reusable pieces keep design consistent and code short.
explanation.sw: Vipande vinavyotumika tena hudumisha muundo na kupunguza msimbo.

quiz.question: Which property rounds the corners of the card?

explanation.en: border-radius rounds corners; 12px is a soft look.
explanation.sw: border-radius huzungusha pembe; 12px ni mwonekano laini.

lessons.title: CSS Variables & Theming
lessons.content: CSS custom properties (--name) store reusable values that can be swapped at runtime, powering features like dark mode without duplicating styles.
lessons.notes: Custom properties cascade like any other CSS property, so scope them thoughtfully.
lessons.mistakes: Defining variables inside a selector that never matches the elements you need.
lessons.practice: Define two color variables and use them across three selectors.
lessons.challenge: Override one variable inside a .dark class to build a mini theme switch.

quiz.question: How do you declare a CSS custom property?

explanation.en: Custom properties start with -- and are read with var().
explanation.sw: Custom property huanza na -- na husomwa kwa var().

quiz.question: How do you use it?

explanation.en: var(--name) reads the value.
explanation.sw: var(--jina) husoma thamani.

quiz.question: Why are variables great for dark mode?
options: They make pages smaller than HTML
Swap values in one place and every use updates

hint.sw: Badilisha mara moja, kila mahali kunasasishwa.

explanation.en: Redefine variables under .dark and all components follow.
explanation.sw: Fafanua upya variables chini ya .dark na vipengele vyote vinafuata.

lessons.title: Advanced Grid Patterns
lessons.content: grid-template-areas lets you name regions of a layout and place elements declaratively, making complex responsive layouts far easier to read and adjust.
lessons.notes: Renaming areas per breakpoint is a clean way to reorganize layout responsively.
lessons.mistakes: Mismatching area names between grid-template-areas and grid-area on children.
lessons.practice: Build a header/sidebar/main/footer layout using named grid areas.
lessons.challenge: Redefine the areas for a single-column layout inside a media query.

quiz.question: What does grid-template-areas let you do?
options: Name regions and place items declaratively

hint.en: Names such as header and sidebar.

explanation.en: You describe the layout like a map.
explanation.sw: Unaelezea mpangilio kama ramani.

quiz.question: Which property assigns an item to a named area?

explanation.en: grid-area links the element to the named region.
explanation.sw: grid-area huunganisha kipengele na eneo lililopewa jina.

quiz.question: A clean way to reorganise layout on mobile:
options: Redefine the areas inside a media query

explanation.en: Changing template areas per breakpoint rearranges the layout.
explanation.sw: Kubadilisha areas kwa breakpoint hupanga upya mpangilio.

lessons.title: Keyframe Animations
lessons.content: @keyframes defines multi-step animations that run independently of user interaction, useful for loaders, entrance effects and ambient motion.
lessons.notes: Respect prefers-reduced-motion so animations don't cause discomfort for sensitive users.
lessons.mistakes: Animating expensive properties like width/height instead of transform/opacity.
lessons.practice: Create a fade-in keyframe animation for a card on page load.
lessons.challenge: Wrap the animation in a prefers-reduced-motion media query.

quiz.question: What does @keyframes define?

explanation.en: Keyframes describe how properties change over time.
explanation.sw: Keyframes zinaeleza jinsi properties zinavyobadilika kwa muda.

quiz.question: How do you apply it to an element?

explanation.en: The animation shorthand names the keyframes and sets timing.
explanation.sw: animation hutaja keyframes na kuweka muda.

quiz.question: Why respect prefers-reduced-motion?
options: Motion can cause discomfort for some users

explanation.en: Reduce or disable animations for those who ask.
explanation.sw: Punguza au zima animation kwa wanaoomba.

lessons.title: Scalable CSS Architecture
lessons.content: As stylesheets grow, naming conventions like BEM (Block__Element--Modifier) keep styles predictable and prevent one component's CSS from silently breaking another's.
lessons.notes: WaiTech's own wtca- prefix strategy is a real-world example of scoping to avoid collisions.
lessons.mistakes: Nesting selectors so deeply that specificity becomes unmanageable.
lessons.practice: Rename a set of classes to follow BEM conventions.
lessons.challenge: Refactor an overly specific selector chain into a single flat class.

quiz.question: What does BEM stand for?

explanation.en: BEM is a naming convention for predictable CSS.
explanation.sw: BEM ni kanuni ya majina kwa CSS inayotabirika.

quiz.question: In .wtca-card--featured, what is the '--featured' part?

explanation.en: -- marks a modifier of the block.
explanation.sw: -- huashiria modifier ya block.

quiz.question: Why prefix or scope class names?
options: Prevent one component's CSS breaking another

explanation.en: Scoping avoids accidental overrides in big stylesheets.
explanation.sw: Scoping huzuia kubatilishana kwa bahati mbaya.

lessons.title: Render Performance
lessons.content: Animating transform and opacity can run on the compositor thread without triggering expensive layout recalculations, unlike animating width, top, or margin.
lessons.notes: will-change hints the browser to optimize upcoming changes, but should be used sparingly.
lessons.mistakes: Overusing will-change on many elements, which can hurt performance instead of helping.
lessons.practice: Rewrite a width-based hover animation to use transform: scale instead.
lessons.challenge: Identify one property in an existing stylesheet that could be swapped for a cheaper equivalent.

quiz.question: Which properties are cheapest to animate?

explanation.en: They can run on the compositor thread.
explanation.sw: Zinaweza kukimbia kwenye compositor thread.

quiz.question: Why avoid animating width or margin?

hint.en: Layout must be recomputed each frame.

explanation.en: Layout changes can cause jank.
explanation.sw: Mabadiliko ya layout yanaweza kusababisha mtetemo.

quiz.question: How should will-change be used?
options: Sparingly, as a hint for upcoming changes

explanation.en: Overuse hurts performance.
explanation.sw: Matumizi kupita kiasi hudhuru utendaji.
